The Contract Is the Beginning

The signature closes a negotiation. It also begins the relationship that determines whether the agreement succeeds.

21 July 20264 min read
TrustRelationshipsLeadership

A signed contract can feel like the finish line. After months of discussion, negotiation and revision, the document is finally complete.

But in my experience, the signature is not the end of the work. It is the beginning of a different kind of work.

Customers rarely remember every clause that was negotiated. They remember whether working with you made their job easier. They remember whether you returned the difficult call, stayed close when something went wrong, and followed through when no one was watching.

The strongest commercial relationships are built after the excitement of winning has passed. They are built through delivery, consistency and the quiet confidence that someone has one less thing to worry about because you are involved.

A contract records the agreement. Trust determines what that agreement becomes.
